newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore GIC seeks to recover investment losses.
newsitem.headline: Singapore GIC seeks to recover investment losses.

text.p: The Government of Singapore Investment Corp (GIC) is seeking to recover losses arising from a case involving investments made through a Hong Kong asset management firm, Finance Minister Richard Hu said.
"The GIC has incurred some loss in its investments made through Rockefeller & Co (Far East) and is in the process of ascertaining the amount," Hu said on Monday in response to queries in parliament.

Pressed to disclose the size of the losses, Hu said that since the investigations involved transactions over several years and were quite complex, "it would not be desirable to make any broad estimates".
"As soon as we have the information, it will be made public," he said.
Singapore government prosecutors charged a regional manager of GIC, Taw Cheng Kong, on November 2 with eight counts of corruption involving at least HK$12 million, the state prosecutor said.
The charge sheet in the case alleged that Taw had received bribes from Kevin Lee Kwok-wing, then managing director of Rockefeller & Co (Far East). Lee himself was not charged.
In Hong Kong, Rockefeller & Co's managing director Colin Moore was not immediately available for comment.
Taw, who has since been suspended by GIC, was not asked to plead and his case will next be mentioned -- or come up in court -- in January.
Hu said the amount involved was small relative to the total funds managed.
He said the risk of such investments was relatively low and "this was the the first significant case that we have come across".
